Understanding Indian temple architecture

An online course of four sessions on the forms and development of the Indian temple

Made for your group

  • Your day and start time, weekends and special days included
  • Any group size, from one person to a whole class
  • Your pace and your language: English, Hindi or both

Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and location. We adapt the length, level and language, and prepare a quotation. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

An introduction to the parts of a temple, the regional styles and their chronology, and the methods scholars use to study architecture. A certificate of completion can be issued.

The course is run for your batch on dates you choose. Timings, pace and assessment are agreed before it begins.

What it covers

  • The parts of a temple and their names
  • The regional styles and how old each is
  • The ways scholars study architecture
  • A certificate of completion, if you want one

Course outline

  1. 1. Vocabulary & sources

    Sanctum, mandapa, superstructure, textual and material evidence.

    You: label a temple plan

  2. 2. Regional development

    Survey early buildings and Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Deccan diversity.

    You: compare three plans

  3. 3. Architecture in context

    Sculpture, patronage, inscription and ritual movement.

    You: interpret selected images

  4. 4. Case-study clinic

    Work through Khajuraho, Pattadakal and Kalinga case studies.

    You: submit annotated building analysis

The number and length of sessions are agreed with your batch.

By the end you can

  • Name the parts of a temple, such as the sanctum, mandapa and superstructure.
  • Compare Nāgara, Drāviḍa and Deccan temples and place the regional styles in chronological order.
  • Analyse a building through case studies of Khajuraho, Pattadakal and Kalinga temples.

You take away

A portfolio of your work from each session.
